title: PACAREA Battle Watch Command Center Display System (CCDS)
description: The U.S. Coast Guard is soliciting for a Battle Watch Command Center Display System (CCDS) Integration for U.S. Coast Guard Pacific Area (PACAREA), Alameda, CA. detailed in the attached Statement of Work (SOW). This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. The size standard is $34 Million and NAICS is 541512. The contract type will be a firm fixed price purchase order. The Government proposes to solicit quotes for the following item(s): Battle Watch Command Center Display System (CCDS) Integration (See attached Statement of Work (SOW) for complete details). 1. Please read the entire solicitation, including all attachments, to ensure completion of all required representations, certifications, and submissions. Acknowledge all Solicitation amendments (SF-30) issued by the Government. 2. Your offer shall include ALL of the documents and information listed in the solicitation; and your offer shall be received by this office at or before September 20, 2026, 8:00 a.m., Pacific Time, to be eligible for award. 3. Submit your offer, with all required documentation to Contracting Specialist, Elizabeth Tam-Hurley at Elizabeth.h.tam-hurley@uscg.mil DO NOT CONTACT ANYONE LISTED IN THE SOW FOR ANY REASON. The POC to request a site visit is: Jacob Dupree, (510) 437-3701. 4. This solicitation does not obligate the Government to compensate for any costs incurred by the Offeror in preparation and/or submission of any offer, not does it obligate the Government to procure for said services/supplies. 5. Questions/Concerns: It shall be the obligation of the offeror to exercise due diligence to discover and to bring to the attention of the Government any ambiguities, inconsistencies, or concerns regarding the information in this solicitation. All question/concerns regarding this solicitation shall be submitted in writing (NO phone calls) to Contracting Specialist, Elizabeth Tam-Hurley at Elizabeth.h.tam-hurley@uscg.mil no later than September 14, 2026, 8:00 AM Pacific Time. Follow up/additional questions will not be accepted after this date. Offerors shall reference the solicitation number and provide enough information in their e-mail so the government can easily respond to their questions/concerns. All questions/concerns will be compiled and addressed on an "Amendment of Solicitation" (SF-30) and will be posted on the SAM.gov website for viewing by all potential offerors. *Only send questions/concerns to the Contracting Officer listed above. AWARD: The Government intends to award a contract to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value, price and other factors considered. title: G002--NEW - Catholic Priest Services - 676
description: The Great Lakes Acquisition Center (GLAC) in Milwaukee, WI is searching for vendors who have the capability to provide Catholic Priest Services to Tomah VAMC, 500 E. Veterans Street Tomah, WI 54660-3105 as stated below, starting 03/01/2027. This is for Market Research purposes only. Chaplain duties will include but not be limited to the following: The contracted Catholic Priest shall be on the Tomah VAMC campus weekly to provide one Catholic Mass service for Catholic Veterans. Contractor shall be an Ordained Catholic Priest who possesses an ecclesiastical endorsement, from the official national endorsing authority of their faith group or denomination. The ecclesiastical endorsement is a written official statement, by the official national endorsing body of the faith group or denomination, certifying that the applicant is in good standing with the applicant's group or denomination; and stating that the individual is, in the opinion of the endorsing body, qualified to perform the full range of ministry required in the VA pluralistic setting. B. The Ordained Catholic Priest shall have the training of their religious faith group that is in keeping with their established standards. C. The contractor who performs the services covered by this contract shall be proficient in written and spoken English. D. Contractor shall have experience working within the VA hospital setting and/or other hospital settings.

title: APN CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR WAINWRIGHT BASE PROGRAM CFB WAINWRIGHT
description: Advance Procurement Notice Construction Management Services for: Wainwright Base Program CFB Wainwright, Alberta (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. This is an advance notice for a potential contract with anticipated security requirements to provide interested Contractors an opportunity to begin the sponsorship process for obtaining (if required) the anticipated security clearance(s). Note that there is no guarantee that this solicitation will proceed or that any security clearance(s) will be granted under the sponsorship process in a timely fashion or otherwise. This project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services The delivery method for this project will be Construction Management. This project will address infrastructure requirements to upgrade the Base Administration Area to meet the current and future needs of the Canadian Armed Forces at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright, Alberta. The intended scope of this work for this project should the project proceed will include: Building Infrastructure: Construction of new buildings to support accommodations, training, warehousing and administration requirements. Renewal of Existing Buildings: Upgrades to existing buildings to extend their lifespan and improve the existing conditions for users. Demolition: Demolition of existing buildings that have been deemed end of life that will be replaced with new infrastructure. Horizontal Asset Improvements: Modification and development of utilities, roads and parking lots in the support of new infrastructure. The estimated cost is in the order of $525,000,000. It is anticipated that this solicitation will be initated in July/August 2026. This is conditional on receiving approval to proceed by the Department of National Defence (DND). Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 86945; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has  met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal or a bid DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. title: Ireland – Digital mapping services – An Area Monitoring System Service
description: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) is issuing this tender competition to enter into a contract with a vendor to supply an Area Monitoring System (AMS) Service within DAFM which has the capacity to deliver the obligations of Article 70 of Regulation 2021/2116 which requires the continued delivery of an AMS service. Article 65 of 2021/2116 defines an area monitoring system as a procedure of regular and systematic observation, tracking and assessment of agricultural activities and practices on agricultural areas by Copernicus Sentinels satellite data or other data of at least equivalent value. It is the intent of this tender competition to solicit proposals from all interested vendors possessing expertise to provide an AMS solution to accommodate the needs of the Area Monitoring and Land Systems Division, within the guidelines established in the tender documents.

description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Clinical Center (CC), Office of Purchasing and Contracts, intends to award a sole-source firm-fixed-price purchase order to Trilogy Innovations, Inc. for Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Engine (OKE) and Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) software subscriptions and associated deployment support. The requirement includes 40 Core Band subscriptions of Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Engine, Premium, Confirmed Stateside Support (SKU MW01016) and six Physical or Virtual Nodes of Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server with Satellite, Premium (SKU RH00008). The subscriptions include Premium Confirmed Stateside Support and are transferable within NIH's internal infrastructure. In addition to the software subscriptions, Trilogy Innovations will provide up to 20 hours of expert-level engineering services to support the initial deployment and configuration of Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Engine within the NIH environment. Services include installation, initial configuration and system readiness, operationalization of the environment for NIH workloads, identification of technical gaps and requirements necessary to support PAS-X onboarding and production readiness, review of the NIH PAS-X OKE environment architecture, and knowledge transfer and configuration documentation, as required. This acquisition is required to support the NIH Clinical Center's transition from paper-based processes and the unsupported StemLab application to the PAS-X application. The current StemLab application has not been supported by its vendor since June 2022. The Clinical Center must comply with strict manufacturing, documentation, and reporting requirements, including requirements applicable to the manufacture and distribution of human cells, tissues, and cellular and tissue-based products. The Red Hat licenses and deployment support will provide the infrastructure necessary for implementation of PAS-X and support the transition from the existing paper-based environment to electronic recordkeeping. Without this acquisition, the program would continue to operate at risk and may be unable to satisfy applicable federal and state requirements. The Government intends to procure this requirement from Trilogy Innovations, Inc. on a sole-source basis. The program office contacted Red Hat regarding the requirement, and Red Hat directed the program office to Trilogy Innovations as the third-party reseller for this acquisition. Trilogy will provide the Red Hat software subscriptions as a pass-through from Carahsoft Technology Corporation/Red Hat, Inc. and will perform the required deployment support. This contract will be for one year. RESPONSE TO NOTICE This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. Description of Action and Proposed Contractor The Special Operations Command South (SOCSOUTH), located at Homestead Air Reserve Base, Florida, intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price purchase order under solicitation number H9228126QE014 pursuant to the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 (Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements), to TacMed Solutions, LLC, located at 1250 Harris Bridge Road, Anderson, SC 29621-1250 (CAGE Code: 3P1B8, UEI: WDK1HVNUA8J4). C. Description of Supplies and Operational Capabilities The proposed procurement encompasses ten (10) each of Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) 0001, xFRIDGE� Expeditionary Refrigerator System, Part Number 103979 (NSN: 4110-01-716-0048), with each system comprising the refrigeration unit with 25 liters of internal storage capacity, AC power cable, DC power cable, cable storage pouch, two BB-2590 rechargeable batteries, and operations manual, with direct delivery to SOCSOUTH, Homestead, FL 33039. The procurement also includes five (5) each of CLIN 0002, Spare High-Capacity Rechargeable Battery (BB-2590 HC), Part Number 102810, with direct delivery to SOCSOUTH, Homestead, FL 33039. Key salient characteristics require that the units provide a minimum of 25 liters of internal volume capable of maintaining tight temperature tolerances (1�C to 6�C) for whole blood and biological products, operate continuously on standard military BB-2590 batteries with integrated dual-battery management and on-board charging capability from external AC/DC power sources, and feature a ruggedized transportable Pelican-case form factor engineered for operational tactical environments and expeditionary field medicine. D. Statutory Authority, Technical Justification, and Fleet Standardization This action is conducted under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, which provides that full and open competition need not be provided for when the supplies or services required by the agency are available from only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Regarding fleet standardization and inventory baseline, SOCSOUTH currently maintains, supports, and operates an existing fielded inventory of TacMed xFRIDGE� units across its operational components. Procuring matching TacMed xFRIDGE� units is necessary to ensure direct compatibility and interoperability with the command's existing cold-chain assets. Introducing an alternate or non-standard refrigeration model would break fleet commonality, create supply-chain inefficiencies, require duplicative spare parts inventories, and necessitate separate training pipelines and operational maintenance protocols for deployed medical personnel. Regarding airworthiness and flight safety integration, the TacMed xFRIDGE� system has demonstrated compliance with military flight safety standards, holding active Airworthiness Releases (AWR) from the U.S. Army Aviation and Missile Command and Flight Clearances from the Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) for operational use aboard designated military aircraft platforms, including CH-53, MH-53, C-130, and V-22. Utilizing equipment with established airworthiness approvals is critical to mission readiness and avoids flight safety hazards and costly testing delays. E. Submission of Capability Statements and Procedures This is a notice of intent and not a request for competitive proposals or quotations. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. Submissions must provide clear and convincing documentation proving that the offered product meets all salient characteristics and agency operational constraints, including full physical, mechanical, operational, and logistical interchangeability with SOCSOUTH's existing fielded inventory of TacMed xFRIDGE� refrigeration equipment without requiring separate maintenance configurations, spare parts lines, or user re-training, as well as verified documentation of active military Airworthiness Releases (AWR) / NAVAIR Flight Clearances for operational use aboard the specified aircraft platforms. Any responses received will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether conducting a competitive procurement is in the best interest of the Government. F. Response Deadline and Points of Contact The deadline for response submission is 20 September 2026 at 16:00 Eastern Time. Interested parties must submit capability statements electronically via email with the subject line "Response to Notice of Intent H9228126QE014 - Expeditionary Refrigerators" to Primary Point of Contact Aisha Ross at aisha.j.ross.mil@socom.mil and Secondary Point of Contact Molly Miller at molly.l.miller.mil@socom.mil. Physical inquiries may be addressed to Special Operations Command South (SOCSOUTH), 29401 SW 125th Ave, Homestead, FL 33039.

title: Tampere (Ranta-Tampella) - Nokia (Harjuniitty) lisäraiteet, ympäristövaikutusten arviointi ja ratatekninen suunnitelma sekä ratasuunnitelma välille Tampere (Lielahti) – Nokia (Harjuniitty)
description: Tampere (Ranta-Tampella) - Nokia (Harjuniitty) lisäraiteet, ympäristövaikutusten arviointi ja ratatekninen suunnitelma sekä ratasuunnitelma välille Tampere (Lielahti) – Nokia (Harjuniitty) Hankinta sisältää Tampere (Ranta-Tampella) – Nokia (Harjuniitty) rataosuuden lisäraiteiden ympäristövaikutusten arvioinnin ja yleissuunnitelmatasoisen ratateknisen suunnitelman laatimisen sekä Tampere (Lielahti) – Nokia (Harjuniitty) rataosuuden ratasuunnitelman laatimisen. Valtion ja Tampereen kaupunkiseudun välisessä MAL sopimuksessa vuosille 2024–2027 on sovittu Epilän ja Harjuniityn seisakkeiden suunnittelusta. Seisakkeet sijaitsevat hankealueella ja sisältyvät optiona suunnittelukokonaisuuteen. Lisäraiteesta on laadittu aluevaraussuunnitelma vuonna 2015 osana laajempaa kokonaisuutta Tampere-Lielahti-Nokia/Ylöjärvi. Vuonna 2020 valmistuneessa Tampere-Pori tarveselvityksessä on hanke esitetty kolmanneksi tärkeimmäksi kehittämistoimenpiteeksi etenkin, jos lähijunaliikenne seudulla kasvaa. Tärkeimmiksi tunnistetut kehittämistoimet on toteutettu rataosalla jo aiemmin. Tarveselvityksen jälkeen on rataosuudella lisätty ostoliikenteen lähijunavuoroja Nokialle. Tesoman seisake on valmistunut vuonna 2021 ja Nokian liikennepaikan kehittämistyöt vuonna 2025. Rauman seisakkeen rakennustyöt ovat käynnissä ja lisävuorot Raumalta Tampereelle on käynnistymässä vuonna 2027. Epilän seisakkeen esiselvitys valmistuu keväällä 2026. Harjuniityn seisakkeen esiselvitys on laadittu aiemmin kaavatyön yhteydessä. Tesoman seisakkeen vaiheittainen toteutus ja lisäraide on huomioitu seisakkeen lainvoimaisessa ratasuunnitelmassa (4.9.2020). Nokian liikennepaikan kehittämisen yhteydessä on selvitetty lisäraiteen sijoittuminen liikennepaikan kohdalla ja tältä osin aluevaraussuunnitelmaa on päivitetty vuonna 2021 julkaistussa liikennepaikan esiselvityksessä. Tampereen ja Nokian yleiskaavoissa lisäraidetarpeet on huomioitu kaavatyön yhteydessä. Asemakaavoissa lisäraidetarpeet on huomioitu varauksina niiltä osin, missä kaavamuutoksia on maankäytön kehittymisen seurauksena ollut tarve päivittää. Nokialla kuntarajalla, Kankaantakana ja Haavistossa on yhteensä n. 1 km hankealuetta asemakaavoittamatta. Palveluntuottajaksi valitaan yksi toimittaja. Hankinnan sisältö on määritelty tarkemmin tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa.,

description: 1. NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER This is a Sources Sought Notice and Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a formal Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Invitation for Bid (IFB). Additional information may be requested after initial response, either from individual respondents or all respondents. 2. PURPOSE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, on behalf of Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), is conducting market research to support acquisition of an estimated $300M MATOC to support Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) construction efforts. This Market Research will help USACE determine the availability and capabilities of firms working within this NAICS code. The responses to this Notice will also be used to help determine whether a small business or socio-economic set-aside may be suitable to apply to this potential procurement. 3. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION The purpose of this MATOC will be to support primarily general construction activities at JBLM and its sub-installations (Lewis Main, McChord Field, and Yakima Training Center), including but not limited to renovation, repairs, minor building expansions and pre-engineered buildings (not to exceed the statutory limit for new construction), preventative maintenance, environmental abatement, erosion control and earthwork. The JBLM FSRM Program includes operational facilities, training sites, administrative spaces, barracks/troop housing, utility infrastructure systems (HVAC, electrical, fire protection), and site work for JBLM Garrison facilities. Projects will span multiple facility types across JBLM. Task Orders under this MATOC are primarily intended to provide a timely procurement response to general construction work such as remediation of facilities, e.g., maintenance, repair, asbestos and lead-based paint abatement, and minor construction situations relating to but not limited to: civil, mechanical, plumbing, structural, electrical, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), and anti-terrorism and force protection. Projects will be primarily general construction activities including but not limited to renovation, repairs, building expansions, and pre-engineered buildings (not to exceed the statutory limit for new construction), or repair by replacement. Scope may also include preventative maintenance, environmental abatement (e.g., asbestos and lead-based paint abatement), erosion control, and earthwork. Construction situations may include but are not limited to civil, mechanical, plumbing, structural, electrical, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), fire protection systems, communications systems, and anti-terrorism and force protection. The MATOC may also be used for Task Orders expected to require some Incidental Design Work or extension of design effort by the Contractor, to include, but not be limited to fire alarm systems, fire sprinkler systems, HVAC system installation and balancing, communications systems, structural design of minor facilities or components and licensed professional engineer certification of site adaptation of pre-engineered structures. 4. POTENTIAL ACQUISITION STRATEGY The USACE Seattle District intends to award a MATOC to offerors determined to be qualified in accordance with the evaluation criteria. Aggregate Program Value: Approximately $300 Million ordering capacity, shared among all MATOC contractors. Structure: Qualified firms will be issued a MATOC contract, establishing a pool of multiple contractors available to support JBLM FSRM. Period of Performance: A 5-year base period with a single two (2) year option period. Exercise of options is at the Government's discretion. Project Size and Task Order Limits: The project size for Task Orders under this MATOC are anticipated to be between $250,000.00 and $25,000,000.00, and the average project duration is expected to be between six months to two years. Based on previous similar contracts, the occurrence of Task Orders may be frequent, especially in emergency situations, and during the 3rd and 4th quarters of the Government�s fiscal year. Project Delivery Methods: Projects will primarily be executed using Design-Bid-Build project delivery, with task orders representing the construction portion of project delivery. Task Order Selection: Competition for task orders will be held among all MATOC participants. Source selection methods will be determined for individual projects and may include various prices, performance, schedule or other trade-offs on the best-value spectrum. 5. ANTICIPATED INDUSTRY DAY USACE Seattle District anticipates hosting an Industry Day in the JBLM area on or about 15 October 2026. Exact date, time, location, registration instructions, and agenda will be published (SAM.gov and/or direct distribution to respondents to this RFI) later. Firms that respond to this RFI will be prioritized for Industry Day communications. 6. Capability statements shall not exceed 5 pages in length. Supplemental capability statements are requested to be submitted via email to the individual(s) listed below no later than 10:00 AM Pacific Time on 20 September 2026. Late responses may still be considered at the Government�s discretion but are not guaranteed review prior to strategy finalization. title: Germany – Supporting services for the government – UNtangling our SEAs (UNSEA) – Ein holistischer Lösungsansatz zur Vermeidung der Belastung der Meeresumwelt mit Fischfanggeräten
description: Trotz eines gewachsenen Bewusstseins der Konsequenzen der Plastikverschmutzung für die marine Umwelt besteht eine anhaltende Bedrohung durch ALDFG, welches neu in die Meeresumwelt eingetragen wird oder sich dort teilweise bereits seit Jahrzehnten befindet. Ziel von UNSEA ist es daher, den weiteren Eintrag von ALDFG in die Nord- und Ostsee sys-tematisch zu verhindern, die negativen ökologischen und sozioökonomischen Auswirkungen zu reduzieren und Altlasten insbesondere in ökologisch sensiblen Gebieten zu identifizieren und zu bergen. Dabei sind sowohl die kommerzielle, die Nebenerwerbs- sowie die Sportfischerei in Nord- und Ostsee zu adressieren. Ausgenommen vom Projektumfang sind Aqua- und Marikulturen und die Binnenfischerei. Existierende Vorgaben und Vereinbarungen relevanter nationaler und internationaler Rechtsvorgaben sind momentan noch fragmentiert, ohne finanziellen Unterbau und stehen teilweise aus verschiedenen Gründen zur Disposition. UNSEA soll daher die verschiedenen Teilaspekte in einem kohä-renten Handlungsrahmen zusammenführen, wobei die Umsetzung kosteneffizienter und operationaler Maßnahmen im Fokus stehen. Dabei gilt es, den Umgang mit Fanggeräteabfällen aus der Fischerei neu und gesamtheitlich zu denken, Prinzipien der Kreislaufwirtschaft im Management von Fischfanggeräten zu verankern und dabei auch spezielle Befunde wie Dolly Ropes (Scheuerschutzfäden an Grundschleppnetzen) und Netzteile aus Reparaturarbeiten zu adressieren, die sich häufig in der Meeresumwelt finden. Das Projekt soll über die Laufzeit die dafür erforderliche Anschubfinanzierung leisten und parallel langfristige Strukturen mit klaren Verantwortlichkeiten für die Verstetigung durch Bund und Länder schaffen. Dabei soll erstmalig ein sek-torübergreifender Mechanismus festgelegt und umgesetzt werden, welcher auch Wissens- und Informationsaustausch beinhaltet. Das Projekt kann auf bestehende rechtliche Rahmenbedingungen, Empfehlungen aus For-schung und Politik, Vorarbeiten im Rahmen von Maßnahmen- und Aktionsplänen und freiwilligen Industrieinitiativen aufbauen. Insbesondere der 2016 etablierte Runde Tisch Meeresmüll (RTM, www.muell-im-meer.de), welcher durch das Umweltbundesamt und das Land Niedersachsen koordiniert wird, hat bereits umfassende konzeptionelle Vorarbeiten geleistet, die als Arbeitsgrundlagen für UNSEA genutzt werden können. Hierüber wurden Erkenntnisse über die Dimension des Problems gewonnen und geeignete Methoden sowie vorhandene und fehlende Elemente in der Kette von der Suche bis zur möglichst um-weltgerechten Verwertung von ALDFG identifiziert. Weiterhin sind die Ergebnisse und Empfehlungen zweier Pilotprojekte zur Umsetzung der Bergung verlorener Fischereigeräte in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern (MV) und Schleswig-Holstein (SH) zu berücksichtigen. Während das Projekt in MV bereits abgeschlossen ist (https://www.wwf.de/fileadmin/fm-wwf/Publikationen-PDF/Deutschland/WWF-Abschlussbericht-Landesprojekt-Verlorene-Fischereigeraete.pdf), wird die Veröffentlichung des Abschlussberichtes des SH-Projektes für August 2026 erwartet mit geplanten Folgeaktivitäten zur Kartierung und Bergung von Fanggeräteabfällen. Die Arbeiten unter UNSEA sollen eng mit diesen Aktivitäten koordiniert werden, um Doppelarbeit zu vermeiden.

Space must be accessible 24 hours a day, 7 days a week and 365 days a year. ? Offered space cannot be collocated with or near other Federal, State and local government agencies or private firms whose primary clientele are involved in or have ties to criminal elements. ? Offered space cannot be collocated or within 1,000 walkable feet of agencies providing probation and/or parole services, halfway house services, drug abuse counseling, rehabilitation programs and similar social services agencies and welfare type programs as well as private law firms representing drug offenders. ? Offered space building entrances/exits cannot to be located within a 1,000 feet 06/2025 minimum boundary of a Drug-free zone or 1,000 walkable feet from a school/park/day care center boundary. ? The space must be capable of meeting Facility Security Level 4 requirements established by the Interagency Security Committee and all Department of Justice site specific requirements. ? The determination of the acceptance of locations where easy surveillance of Government facilities creates an unacceptable security risk to operations is within the sole discretion of the Government. Offered space must meet Government requirements for fire safety, accessibility, seismic, and sustainability standards per the terms of the Lease. A fully serviced lease is required. The Government is considering alternative space if economically advantageous. Tämän tarkoituksena on ilmaista tarjoajille toiminnanohjaukselle asetettavia vähimmäisvaatimuksia. Lisäksi on kuvattu tavoitteita nykytoiminnan kehittämiseksi. Tarkoituksenamme on korvata nykyjärjestelmä ohjelmistopalvelulla (SaaS), joka mahdollistaa prosessien kehittämisen ja turvaa laadullisesti vakaan toiminnan. HUS hakee SaaS-pohjaista ohjelmistopalvelua, jonka tulee pohjautua tuotantokäytössä jo olevaan ja valmiiseen ohjelmistoon ja tilaajalle siitä konfiguroitavaan ratkaisuun. Hanke on suunniteltu aikataulultaan sellaiseksi, että ohjelmistopalvelu otetaan käyttöön vuoden 2028 aikana. Hanke käynnistetään määrittelyvaiheella, jossa tarkennetaan tehdyt kuvaukset voittaneen tarjoajan tarjoamaa ohjelmistopalvelua vasten ja näin varmistetaan, että kyseinen ohjelmistopalvelu täyttää asetetut vaatimukset ja tarjoaa selkeän kehityspolun. Tässä määrittelyvaiheessa myös tarkennetaan käyttöönottoprojektin suunnitelma sellaiselle tasolle, että osapuolet voivat sitoutua projektin toteutukseen. Määrittelyvaihe on aikaperusteisesti laskutettava, maksimissaan 50 000 euroa ja kestoltaan enintään neljä kuukautta. Liitteessä Käyttöönottoprojektin kuvaus on tarkemmin selostettu mitä määrittelyvaiheessa tulee tuottaa. Määrittelyvaiheen jälkeen molemmilla osapuolilla on, niin halutessaan, mahdollisuus luopua hankkeesta.
